front: What are the five disciplined lifecycle phases of a production ML engineering project from scratch to deployment?
back: Problem formulation & metric definition, data hygiene & baseline benchmarking, model iteration & ablation, deployment packaging, and post-launch drift monitoring.
explanation: Shipping production ML requires disciplined baselines (always establish a simple dumb baseline first) before investing in complex architectures.

front: Why must every machine learning project implement a trivial heuristic or simple linear baseline before training complex deep neural networks?
options: To verify data integrity, quantify the true marginal gain of complex models, and detect label leakage early
Because deep networks cannot compile without a baseline checkpoint
To ensure GPU drivers are initialized with floating point numbers
To eliminate the need for cross-validation on test sets
back: To verify data integrity, quantify the true marginal gain of complex models, and detect label leakage early
explanation: If a sophisticated Transformer barely outperforms logistic regression on TF-IDF, the complexity and inference latency may not be justified.

front: Fitting feature scalers, imputers, or tokenizers on the combined dataset before splitting causes data _____ which artificially inflates validation metrics.
explanation: Preprocessors must fit strictly on the training partition alone and only transform validation and test partitions.

front: Why do improvements in offline evaluation metrics (e.g. higher validation AUC or lower perplexity) sometimes fail to translate to online business impact?
back: Offline datasets suffer from survivorship bias, distribution drift, delayed feedback loops, and user behavioral adaptations that static sets cannot reflect.
explanation: Rigorous A/B testing or shadow deployments are necessary to confirm that offline metric improvements yield real-world efficacy.

front: Which set of practices guarantees scientific reproducibility across machine learning experiments?
options: Deterministic random seeding, pinned package lockfiles, dataset version hashes, and tracked experiment hyperparameters
Disabling GPU cache memory and deleting log files after every epoch
Using only random numbers for weight initialization without seeds
Training models exclusively in interactive terminal prompts without recording configs
back: Deterministic random seeding, pinned package lockfiles, dataset version hashes, and tracked experiment hyperparameters
explanation: Pinned environments and exact seeds allow collaborators and CI systems to replicate loss curves and benchmark figures reliably.

front: When training loss continues declining while validation loss begins climbing upwards, the model has entered the _____ regime.
explanation: The model begins memorizing dataset noise rather than learning generalizable underlying patterns, signaling the need for early stopping or regularization.

front: What is the P99 latency SLA in real-time user-facing inference, and why is mean latency insufficient?
back: P99 is the 99th percentile response time; mean latency conceals long tail stalls (GC pauses, queuing delays, KV-cache thrashing) that affect real users.
explanation: A system with 50ms average latency might have 1,500ms P99 spikes. Production SLAs are almost always budgeted against P95 or P99.

front: What is the purpose of an ablation study in a final Capstone research or engineering report?
back: To systematically remove or disable individual components (e.g. data augmentation, attention heads, normalization) to measure each part's actual contribution.
explanation: Ablations isolate which architectural innovations actually drove performance improvements versus what was merely redundant complexity.
